Astarion addresses a defeated Cazador after their fight. He pulls his former master from the coffin where he's recovering and has to decide what to do with him - kill him or carve the scars on Astarion's back into Cazador's and then use him as a sacrifice in the ritual.

Cazador greets Companion or Avatar Astarion in the ritual room, pleased Astarion has returned and he'll finally be able to complete the ritual. The other 6 vampire spawn are in their places for the ritual, ringing the room, held in spectral chains. Astarion starts nervous, but gets angrier as Cazador goads him until Astarion attacks. Cazador uses his magic to immobilise Astarion and then telekinetically flings him into his place (a spot directly behind Cazador) for the ritual, which then begins as the dialog ends and combat starts.

You wake up and find Astarion hunching over you, fangs bared. You fight him off. Caught off guard, he's alarmed and worried that you're going to kill him. He tries to be charming, explaining that he's too weak without blood. If you push back against his excuses he gets frustrated - he tries to bargain with you. If you agree to let him bite you, he's thrilled. He feels in control again. After drinking, he feels invigorated and cocky.

Astarion wakes up from a terrifying dream of his old master. His master had forbidden him to drink humanoid blood, but his master wasn't there... Astarion looks at the sleeping companions and considers biting one of them. If he does, he rolls a stealth check. If he succeeds, he sucks their blood (he can stop or decide to drain them dry). If he fails they wake up, and have to be convinced not to leave him.
Dialog which happens if you defeat Cazador without Astarion and outside the ritual. Ends with a decision whether to free, destroy, or trap the remaining vampire spawn prisoners.
context: You are in Cazador’s ritual chamber after a fight: Astarion has just pulled his former master from an open coffin and thrown him to the floor, with Cazador weakly regaining consciousness and hurling insults. Cazador once carved runes/scars into Astarion that bind him (and many others) to a ritual that will sacrifice those bearing the marks if completed. Astarion now faces a choice — kill Cazador outright, or finish the ritual by transferring the scars and using Cazador as the ritual sacrifice so he can ascend and free himself from the parasite and his fear. The player/companion arguments focus on the moral cost: releasing the bound vampire spawn would endanger countless innocents, while completing the ritual could grant Astarion power and true freedom.
